items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: His name was Beverly Peer. Beverly for the past few years has been the bassist with the great Bobby Short, national and international fame, known greatly on the

ctx.x: time. I said, "The grass is always greener on the other side. You want this, and I'd like to be where you are."

Anyway, when I left, Bobby took the job, and apparently he liked it, because I don't think Bobby has played with an instrumental group since then, and every time I see him, he seems to be quite comfortable with job. And that's 35 years that he's been there. So any time you're on the job that long, there's got to be something about it that you like.

Working with Billy, as far as playing, is a pleasure, because the guy is quite an artist, he knows what he's doing. And I give him a lot of credit, along with Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker and them, for some of the things that I learned from him as an accompanist and about music. Billy and Sarah Vaughan are the two most literate singers that I've worked with, in the sense that they both read music, they know what they're doing, they know the art of singing, and the whole bit.
